newsitem.title: USA: Atlantic Beach, Fla., counsel confirms IRS probe.
newsitem.headline: Atlantic Beach, Fla., counsel confirms IRS probe.

text.p: The bond counsel for the city of Atlantic Beach, Fla., confirmed that the IRS is investigating the city's 1996 water-sewer revenue bond issue but said Wednesday she did not know the focus of the probe.
"I have absolutely no idea," attorney Sandy MacLennan said.
MacLennan said the city had complied with the IRS' request for information about the $22 million issue.

The agency asked for documents relating to the selection of First Union Capital Markets Corp, a unit of First Union Corp, as financial adviser, William R. Hough & Co as lead underwriter, and AMBAC Inc's AMBAC Investment Corp for the deal. AMBAC temporarily invested the bond proceeds until they were needed for construction, MacLennan said.
The selection was made by competitive bid, and at least three bids were received for each post, she said.
"Every T was crossed, every I was dotted," MacLennan said.
The bond issue was validated in the Duval County Circuit Court, and was used to fund court-ordered improvements in the city's sewage and drainage system, she said.
Yield-burning was not an issue because no escrow was involved, MacLennan said.
"It was a current refunded. It refunded a bank loan that was paid off when the bonds were issued, plus a new money piece," MacLennan said.

The Jacksonville Times-Union reported Wednesday that the probe may have been triggered by an Atlantic Beach resident who was a frequent critic of the bond issue and who had complained at city commission meetings that the deal involved unusually high investment fees and commissions. The city has disputed that allegation.
